title: Output hypothesis drift & granular scoring suite for quantized models
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Build a reusable, high-resolution scoring suite that measures subtle output differences introduced by FP8/INT8 quantization and calibration workflows across generative and discriminative tasks. The suite must produce per-task, per-profile, and aggregated quality deltas; support perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy, BLEU/ROUGE, and custom task scorers (e.g., extractive QA F1, summarization pairwise ranking); and integrate with the calibration pipeline so that calibration runs emit structured metric artifacts for CI, dashboards, and rollout gating. The output format must be JSONL rows with stable schema for downstream ingestion by Console and Optimize.
background: Current quant calibration runs produce coarse pass/fail signals and token-level perplexity dumps. Engineers and PMs have asked for finer signals: per-task directionality (hallucination vs brevity), statistical significance of observed deltas, and mapping from profile knobs (per-channel scale, activation clipping thresholds) to task-specific degradations. Existing eval harnesses are scattered across repos and are slow to run end-to-end for comprehensive suites.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical scoring API documented and implemented (scorers.perplexity, scorers.classification, scorers.bleu, scorers.rouge, scorers.f1, scorers.custom_task)
Calibration pipeline emits metrics JSONL with fields: profile_id, quant_backend, seed, dataset_id, metric_name, metric_value, confidence_interval, sample_count
CI job that runs a representative lightweight suite (~5 tasks) completes under 30 minutes for a reference FP8/INT8 profile
Dashboard ingest works and shows per-profile trendlines and significance markers
Canaries fail when quality delta > configured threshold (default: relative drop > 2.0% for accuracy tasks or BLEU/ROUGE absolute drop > 0.5)
tasks: Design stable JSONL schema for scorer outputs and register in docs
Implement scorers library (Python) with adapters for sacrebleu, rouge-score, sklearn metrics
Create a lightweight MMLU-style harness with stratified sampling for quick CI runs
Wire metrics emitter into calibration orchestration so runs attach artifacts to calibration jobs
Add per-profile aggregation service that computes task-weighted deltas and bootstrap CIs
Add CI gating rules and integrate with rollout controller to mark profiles as rejected/accepted
decisions: Use sacrebleu and rouge-score for reference implementations; wrap to provide deterministic tokenization across runs
Perplexity should be reported both raw and normalized by token-length distribution of the baseline dataset
Adopt bootstrap-based confidence intervals (1000 replicates default) to measure significance for small sample tasks
Default task weighting: production tasks get higher weight; provide config file to override per-workload
design_notes: Avoid large monolithic suites in CI: provide a fast 'smoke' profile and a comprehensive nightly profile. The smoke profile uses small stratified shards of each dataset to keep runtime bounded. To detect drift that only appears on long-range contexts, include a dedicated 'long-context' summarization task in nightly runs. Store full scoring outputs in object storage and only push aggregated metrics to the console index to reduce storage costs.
implementation_notes:
- Implement scorer adapter interface: score(predictions_file, references_file, config) -> metric tuples.
- Add deterministic seeding and stable sampling for reproducible CIs.
- Expose a CLI `redwood-score` and a thin gRPC endpoint for orchestrator to call after calibration steps.
- Tag metric outputs with calibration metadata (profile_id, backend, quant_bits, calibration_dataset).
tradeoffs: Computation vs signal: full MMLU suites provide clearer signal but cost ~10x more GPU time — we mitigate via stratified sampling and nightly full runs
Per-task custom scorers increase maintenance cost but are required for domain-specific regressions (e.g., code synthesis correctness)
Bootstrap CIs are compute-heavy but far more robust than analytical approximations given non-iid outputs
risks: False positives in CI gating if baseline variance is underestimated
Tokenization mismatch across libraries could create artificial BLEU/ROUGE deltas
Large-scale nightly runs may overload shared infra if not scheduled or throttled
mitigations: Include baseline re-run job that computes within-baseline variance and updates thresholds periodically
Bundle and pin a tokenizer binary and integrate tokenizer unit tests into scoring library
Add rate limits and queueing for nightly evaluation workers; expose quota lowerings for enterprise customers who want heavier coverage
